**![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Preserve explicit HTML breaks when parsing markdown** For supported markdown containing `
` tags, replacing each tag with an ordinary newline loses the mandatory line break: the paragraph parser subsequently joins those lines with spaces. For example, `one
two
three` becomes a single-line paragraph, so `estimate_markdown()` underestimates its height despite explicitly treating `
` as measurable HTML. Preserve these as hard breaks through paragraph assembly so `_text_lines()` counts the rendered lines. Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

public_comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
public_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound placeholder row allocation by the visible-row cap**

When a caller supplies a large row count with few or no labels, `_row_heights()` allocates and sorts an entry for every data row before applying `max_rows`. Consequently, estimating a table with millions of rows and `max_rows=15` still consumes memory proportional to the entire row count; sufficiently large counts can exhaust the process's memory even though only 15 rows affect the result. Limit the unlabeled placeholder allocation to the cap while retaining the tallest relevant labeled rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

causal_evidence: The base-to-head diff adds sizing.py, including the unbounded placeholder allocation and both public estimator callers, in commit 57b2308b46368d3c1b97100ebe0df4f81088dd59.
supersetapiplus/dashboards/layout/sizing.py:262-271 preserves the full known row count; estimate_table:298 and estimate_pivot_table:312 pass it to _row_heights.
evidences: supersetapiplus/dashboards/layout/sizing.py:258 allocates rows-len(heights) placeholders; line 259 sorts the full list before slicing to max_rows.

Reproduced using .venv/bin/python -B, tracemalloc, and PROFILE loaded from tests/unit/test_layout_sizing.py:25: estimate_table(TableContent(rows=1000000), PROFILE, max_rows=15) peaked at 16000784 traced bytes versus 1600783 bytes for 100000 rows. Both returned units (73, 73, 85).
The same reproduction for estimate_pivot_table peaked at 16000744 traced bytes for 1000000 rows versus 1600743 for 100000 rows, with identical units (75, 75, 100). Labels were empty in every case.
tests/unit/test_layout_sizing.py:92-97 checks capped results with 40 rows but does not check allocation growth.
payload.headline: Visible-row cap does not bound placeholder allocation
payload.before: Known row counts allocate placeholders proportional to the entire dataset before applying max_rows.
payload.after: Bound placeholder allocation by the visible-row cap while preserving the tallest relevant labeled rows.
payload.motivation: Large row counts cause unnecessary linear memory consumption and can exhaust memory despite a small visible-row cap.
payload.reply: Confirmed in both table estimators. With no labels and max_rows=15, increasing rows from 100,000 to 1,000,000 increased traced peak allocation from approximately 1.6 MB to 16 MB without changing the estimated heights. Placeholder allocation must be capped before sorting, preserving the tallest labeled rows.
